sections.h2: Which Macomb County office handles which part of the tax bill?
sections.html:
Three layers split the work. The assessor in each city, township or village sets the assessment. That municipality's treasurer mails the bill and collects it, as MCL 211.44 describes. The Macomb County Treasurer enters the picture only when taxes go unpaid past the local deadline.

The county is the third largest in Michigan, with 881,217 people in 2020 spread over 27 cities, townships and villages and 479 square miles of land. Warren, Sterling Heights and St. Clair Shores are cities, and Armada, New Haven and Romeo are villages. A buyer in Roseville and a buyer in Romeo therefore receive bills from different offices, even though the county treasurer sits behind both.

The county Treasurer's Office answers at 586-469-5190 or treasurer@macombgov.org, weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. Its tax information page separates real property, meaning land and permanent structures, from personal property such as machinery, fixtures and equipment owned by a business. Delinquent real or personal property tax can be paid online with a debit card or ACH, and a GIS search returns legal descriptions from an address or tax ID.

sections.h2: Who can change a Macomb County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the local board of review, because the county cannot do it. The Macomb County Equalization Department (586-469-5260, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.) runs sales and appraisal studies by property class in each city and township to check that local assessments are fair across the county, and it states that it does not determine an individual property's assessment. Its authority is Section 211.34 of the General Property Tax Act.

A protest starts at the board of review, whose first March meeting falls on the second Monday, or the Tuesday or Wednesday after if the local government chose that. Under MCL 211.30 it must hold at least 12 hours of hearings that week, including three hours after 6 p.m. Nonresidents may protest by letter, and local governments may extend that option to residents.

The written decision arrives by the first Monday in June and points to the Michigan Tax Tribunal as the next step, with a filing date printed on the notice. Keep that notice. If you miss the March session, the next opening is the following March.

sections.h2: Will a sale raise the next tax bill on a Macomb County house?
sections.html:
Usually yes. A long-held home carries a taxable value held down by an annual cap, and a sale lifts that value to the state equalized value, which tracks about half the market price, for the next year. The mechanics are in MCL 211.27a. The buyer, not the seller, files the change notice with the assessor, and has 45 days to do it.

Not every transfer counts as a sale for this purpose. The statute exempts:

  • Moves between spouses.
  • Residential transfers to a parent, child, sibling or grandchild that stay non-commercial.
  • Foreclosure transfers, until the lender resells.
  • Court-ordered transfers with no stated price.

For a seller, this means the buyer's carrying cost can differ sharply from yours, and a seller who owned for decades may want to tell a buyer to expect a higher bill. The assessor in your own city or township can quote the current taxable value, and the county Treasurer's tax histories show what has been paid. Sellers handling an estate should check whether the heir is a close relative under the statute, since that decides whether the taxable value resets when title moves out of the decedent's name.

sections.h2: What does the county charge once taxes go delinquent?
sections.html:
On March 1 following the tax year, unpaid real property tax becomes payable to the County Treasurer, with a 4% administration fee and interest at 1% per month. The fee is spelled out in the county's delinquent tax FAQ, which also warns that forfeiture a year later raises the rate to 1.5% per month, applied back to the original delinquency date.

The county describes the sequence as a three-year forfeiture and foreclosure process. The published schedule for 2025 taxes shows how the notices and fees stack up:

Macomb County Treasurer schedule for unpaid 2025 property taxes
DateWhat happens
March 3, 2026Taxes delinquent, 4% fee and 1% interest added
June 1 and September 1, 2026First class mail notices
October 1, 2026$15 fee added
March 1, 2027Forfeiture, $175 minimum title search fee
September 1, 2027Personal visit, $50 fee
January 2028Show cause hearing with the Treasurer
March 31, 2028Foreclosure final, redemption ends

A circuit court hearing in February 2028 produces the foreclosure judgment, and a $35 publication fee is added in November 2027.

sections.h2: How many warnings does a Macomb County owner get before foreclosure?
sections.html:
The county FAQ lists what an owner should receive before foreclosure:

  • Four first class mail notices.
  • Two certified mail notices.
  • Three notices published in a county newspaper.
  • Staff visits to the property beginning each September, repeated until the redemption period expires.

The Treasurer's Office also offers to explain the process, set up a payment plan or point owners to assistance programs through its tax foreclosure prevention page.

Once foreclosure is final, the owner cannot get the property back. It is offered first to the State of Michigan at fair market value, then to the local community, and what remains goes to public auction held between the third Tuesday in July and the first Tuesday in November, with notice published 30 days ahead.

Money left over after an auction can belong to the former owner. For auctions beginning in 2021, anyone who held an interest at the time of foreclosure may file a claim for proceeds above the taxes owed. The county is also taking part in a settlement of claims for surplus proceeds from auctions before 2021, listed on the Treasurer's page as the Fox class action. In the 2025 tax year timeline, the claim deadline is July 1, 2028.

sections.h2: How are back taxes dealt with when selling a Macomb County home?
sections.html:
Request a payoff figure from the Treasurer that runs through the planned closing date, and let the title company settle it out of the seller's proceeds. Interest at 1% per month keeps growing in the first year, so a payoff quoted for the first of a month changes the next month.

The register of deeds will record a warranty deed only with a Treasurer's certificate showing no unpaid tax for the preceding five years, under MCL 211.135. A seller who is still in the first delinquent year has the most room to act, because forfeiture fees such as the $175 title search charge have not yet been added.

Michigan also allows a collecting unit to add up to a 1% administration fee on bills paid before February 15 and a 3% late penalty from February 15 until the bill is returned as delinquent, if the municipality has authorized it. Ask your own city or township treasurer what it charges.

faqs.q: When does Macomb County treat property tax as delinquent?
faqs.a: March 1 of the year after the tax year. For 2025 taxes the county's published date is March 3, 2026, when a 4% fee and 1% interest are added.

faqs.q: Who sets my Macomb County property assessment?
faqs.a: Your city or township assessor does. The county Equalization Department at 586-469-5260 compares assessments across the county and says it does not determine any individual property's assessment.

faqs.q: How long until Macomb County forecloses on unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: About three years. Property is forfeited after the first year, and unpaid taxes as of March 31 in the third year of delinquency lead to foreclosure and title passing to the county treasurer.

faqs.q: Does selling change my Macomb County taxable value?
faqs.a: The seller's value does not carry over to the buyer. After a transfer of ownership, the next year's taxable value is set at the state equalized value, and the buyer reports the transfer to the assessor within 45 days.

faqs.q: Can I recover auction proceeds after a Macomb County tax foreclosure?
faqs.a: Possibly. Former owners and others with an interest can file to claim proceeds above the taxes owed, under the county's published deadlines, and a separate class action settlement covers auctions before 2021.
